title: SAML 2.0 conformance checker and onboarding acceptance criteria
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Build a lightweight SAML 2.0 conformance checker that runs during the interactive SSO setup flow and as a standalone diagnostic tool. The checker validates incoming IdP metadata and the SP<->IdP handshake for common failure modes we see in customer onboarding: missing or malformed ACS/EntityID entries, unsigned metadata, invalid certificates, XML canonicalization variance, NameID/attribute-format mismatches, and clock skew. It should produce actionable, human-readable remediation hints (and suggested config diffs) rather than opaque error codes so support and customers can complete setup without engineering intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard integrates conformance checker: metadata uploaded/URL-entered by admin triggers a preflight check with results surfaced in the UI

Checker detects and categorizes at least 85% of known failure classes (signature issues, certificate chain problems, missing ACS endpoints, entityID mismatches, duplicate AssertionConsumerService indices, invalid NameID formats, encryption-required vs provided), with specific remediation guidance for each
Checker produces a machine-readable 'sanity report' (JSON) that can be attached to support tickets and stored in audit logs
Non-blocking warnings (e.g., expired-but-rotated cert with valid chain) are surfaced separately from blocking errors and include recommended rollback/rotation steps
Automated retries for signed metadata fetch handle up to 2 transient HTTP failures and report timing/HTTP status to observability
Unit and integration tests cover simulated IdP metadata variants and use a small set of representative SAML fixtures
PR merged with code review from security and platform, and staging rollout behind feature flag
implementation_steps: Design JSON schema for sanity report and map it to console UI panels (UX doc in Confluence)
Implement metadata ingestion pipeline: URL fetch, local upload, HTTP retry/backoff, size and XML well-formedness checks
Add SAML parser checks: entityID normalization, ACS matching, SingleLogout endpoints, NameID/attribute-format validation
Verify signature presence and validate XML signatures and certificate chains (OCSP/CRL not required in MVP but log cert validity and expiration)
Produce human-friendly hints with suggested config diff snippets (example: replace 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress' with '...:transient' if mismatched)
Wire results into wizard UX: expanding details, copyable remediation snippet, and a 'Run again' button
Add server-side endpoint to export the sanity report for support and to attach to audit logs
Feature-flag rollout, staging smoke tests, and canary on 10% of new SSO setups
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with PM and Design — aligned on user flows and error messaging tone (friendly, prescriptive)
2025-02-14: PoC parser implemented (Go) that validates entityID and ACS entries against 6 test fixtures — passed basic checks
2025-02-16: UX mockups delivered (Confluence link) showing inline remediation snippets and copy-to-clipboard for config diffs
2025-02-18: Added XML signature validation and certificate chain checks; discovered XProc-style namespace edge-case in one fixture and added a normalization step
2025-02-20: First full integration test against synthetic IdP scenarios — failing cases classified and remediation text drafted
decisions: MVP will not perform OCSP checks or contact remote CRL endpoints to avoid network timeouts during wizard flow; instead, we will log expiry and encourage rotation
Sanity report format chosen as compact JSON lines to allow easy ingestion into existing audit and support systems
Checker will run synchronously in the wizard but with a 6s hard timeout — on timeout we return partial results and a clear 'retry from console' action
We will store only the sanitized metadata fingerprint and the generated sanity report in audit logs; raw metadata full XML will be omitted by default for privacy unless admin opts-in
open_risks: Edge-case metadata that relies on non-standard XML canonicalization may produce false negatives — requires manual support intervention
Time-limited synchronous check may still block some slow IdP endpoints; need fallback UX that permits 'dry run later'
Storing metadata fingerprints without full XML might hinder advanced debugging for support if customer declines opt-in
qa_plan: Run the full fixture suite in CI with 12 synthetic IdP variants. Add end-to-end smoke tests in staging that exercise cloud-hosted IdP endpoints. QA to validate UI messages and copy, and to confirm that the 'attach report' button includes the JSON sanity report without sensitive metadata by default.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: enable for internal orgs -> partner orgs (2 customers) -> 10% canary of newly created customers -> full rollout after 2 weeks and no critical incidents. Monitor support ticket rate for SSO setups and sanity-report download counts.
